learning_objective: 🎯 Step into the shoes of a sociologist! Learn the scientific tools and methods used to study people, decode society, and gather facts without bias.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Objectivity means looking at facts without personal bias, emotions, or prejudices. Subjectivity relies on personal feelings and opinions. Sociologists strive for objectivity but recognize it's hard because they are part of the society they study.
Macro methods (like surveys) study large groups and broad trends across society. Micro methods (like participant observation) study small groups or face-to-face interactions in deep detail.
A method where the researcher lives with the group being studied, doing what they do, to understand their culture from the 'inside'. It is deeply detailed but takes months or years to complete.

A survey asks questions to a large number of people to gather statistical data. Since asking everyone in a country is impossible, researchers use a 'Sample'—a small, representative group chosen to reflect the whole population.
A guided conversation to collect data. 'Structured' interviews have fixed, pre-written questions (like a verbal form). 'Unstructured' interviews are flexible and flow like a natural conversation.

fun_activity.title: 🥧 The Soup Sampling Test
fun_activity.instructions: How do you know if a huge pot of soup has enough salt? You don't drink the whole pot—you stir it and taste one spoonful! That one spoonful is your 'Sample'. That's exactly how sociologists use a sample to understand a population!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly explain the problem of 'Objectivity' in sociology: the researcher is a human studying other humans, so staying 100% unbiased is a challenge.
📌 Contrast Participant Observation (deep, slow, micro) with Surveys (broad, fast, macro).
📌 Define a 'Representative Sample'—a sample that accurately reflects the diversity of the larger population.
quick_recap: ⭐ Quantitative research deals in numbers (Surveys), Qualitative deals in meanings/experiences (Interviews/Observation).
⭐ The researcher must maintain 'reflexivity'—constantly checking their own biases during the study.
⭐ Doing sociology requires a toolkit of multiple methods, as no single method is perfect for everything.
